title: Who Can Restore Access?
briefing: Earlier service isolation has removed compromised credentials but locked some residents out of benefits and permits. Community groups warn that the same checks exclude people whose records were lost.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: A clean credential directory is ready, but importing old account links would reintroduce the pathway used by the intrusion.
private_intelligence.community: Residents with changed names or shared phones fail the automated checks most often and cannot wait weeks for benefits.
private_intelligence.economy: Manual identity desks cost more per case; a frozen benefit also costs local shops immediate purchasing power.
private_intelligence.safety: Emergency one-time access can restore urgent prescriptions, but repeat use must be checked to prevent diverted supplies.

choices.title: Use Strict Digital Reissue
choices.description: Restore only accounts that pass the clean digital checks.
choices.consequence: The new directory remains dependable and low-cost, but excluded residents face interrupted access and legitimacy falls.

choices.title: Fund Supervised Recovery Desks
choices.description: Issue reviewed credentials through neighborhood identity desks.
choices.consequence: Residents regain a usable route and urgent needs are screened, while manual review consumes staff and money.

choices.title: Grant Temporary Basic Access
choices.description: Allow limited benefits while full identity records are rebuilt.
choices.consequence: Purchasing power and basic access recover quickly, but unresolved account links and diversion risks persist.
